name: Roland XPS-60
description: Roland XPS-60 expandable synthesizer: the temporary scene (common, IFX, chorus, reverb, vocoder, arpeggio, and the Part, EQ, MFX, Zone and Arpeggio blocks of parts 1, 2 and R), part 1's temporary tone (four partials with envelopes, LFOs, EQs and the synth layer), the rhythm part's drum kit with all 88 keys, and the system settings.

sources.title: XPS-60 MIDI Implementation (version 1.02, Jan. 14, 2025)
sources.notes: Parameter Address Map read by tools/profiles/roland/parse-address-map.mjs from XPS-60_MIDI_Imple_eng01_W.pdf (sha256 d9591ce3a126cda7f9ada1750a73720390b8595e2de24bfed656fd36e2b1df59). Model ID 01 06 09, DT1 = 12, RQ1 = 11, Roland checksum. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/roland/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/roland/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is the manual's, at the manual's address, with the manual's name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

Scene parts: the profile has the Part, EQ, MFX, Zone and Arpeggio blocks of all eight parts, 1-7 and Part R (the rhythm part). The manual's [Scene] table (p15) prints only "(Part 1)", "(Part 2)", ":" and "(Part R)"; Parts 3-7 are filled in from the stride.

Part 1's tone is at 02 00 00 00. A tone is one type (common, MFX, PMT, four partials with envelopes, LFO and EQ, and the synth layer), so Part 1 has no alternative tone types to keep out of the startup read.

The drum kit (03 00 00 00) is the rhythm part's: seven Temporary Tones for Part 1-7, one Temporary Drum Kit, and an eighth part, R. Key k's partial is at 03 00 16 00 + (k-21) x 00 01 00 and its partial EQ at 03 00 6E 00 + (k-21) x 00 01 00 (7-bit carry).

[Tone PMT] (p95) prints partial 1's velocity range as "VeloRange Lower" and partials 2-4's as "Velocity Range Lower", so the generator numbers only the last three: part1.tone.pmt.velorangeLower is partial 1, velocityRangeLower1-3 are partials 2-4. Every other PMT row is numbered 1-4 by partial.

Tone Partial's four matrix controls print "Source n" once and "Destination 1-4" / "Sens 1-4" under each; the generator numbers the repeats by matrix control, so destination12 is Matrix Control 2's Destination 1 (as in the JUNO-X profile).

Partial LFO prints its two LFOs' rows without an LFO number; the generator numbers each repeat in printed order, so the last digit is the LFO: waveform1 is LFO 1's Waveform, step52 is LFO 2's Step 5, step16Curve1 is LFO 1's Step 16 Curve. "Delay Time Keyfolow" is the manual's spelling.

Presets list the scenes (Bank Select MSB 85), recalled on the profile's channel, which should be the System's Scene Control Channel. Tones (MSB 71/87) and drum kits (MSB 70/86) are chosen per part and are not listed.

Manual: the sentence on p8 says "The model ID of the exclusive messages used by this instrument is 01H 05H 0AH" (the JUNO-D's), and so does the worked example on p114; the RQ1 and DT1 byte tables (p8-9, p13-14) and the address map heading (p15) give 01 06 09, which is used.
Manual: Scene Common Category (p20) is printed on a "0000 aaaa" field (0-15) with the range 0-32 and thirty-three labels; kept as the range and labels print it.
Manual: the Tone Bank Select table (p1) labels MSB 071 / LSB 065-066 "RR-B"; read as PR-B.

The Temporary Drum Kit Inst (03 30 00 00) is a single drum instrument, and the manual (p16) does not say which key's instrument it holds or when the instrument answers for it; an RQ1 it cannot answer gets nothing back ("If the conditions are not met, nothing is transmitted", p8), and the startup read stops at the first request that is not answered. So it is read on request. Part 1 needs no such care: a tone is one type, and the kit is the rhythm part's, which always has one.

No example message is checked: The only printed DT1 example (p114, "Setting scene level to 74") prints F0 41 10 01 05 0A 12 01 00 00 11 4A 24 F7: the JUNO-D's model ID 01 05 0A, where this manual's RQ1/DT1 byte tables (p8-9, p13-14) and its address map heading (p15) give 01 06 09, as the XPS-10X's example (its p112) does. The address, value and checksum agree with the map; the bytes as printed cannot be what this profile sends, so the example is not claimed.
Not read at startup (read on request, since the instrument may not answer them): drumKit.inst.

coverage.inboundControllers: not modelled: what the front panel transmits is in the Control Change section, not the address map
coverage.effectParameterMeanings: type-dependent: MFX, IFX, chorus, reverb and vocoder parameters are Roland's 4-nibble container (12768-52768, shown -20000..+20000); what each slot does depends on the selected type, which the MIDI Implementation does not list
coverage.sceneParts: all eight parts, 1-7 and R. The [Scene] offset table (p15) prints each per-part list as "(Part 1)", "(Part 2)", ":", "(Part R)"; the map fills Parts 3-7 in from the stride, since the run closes on Part R.
coverage.partTones: part 1 only: Temporary Tone (Part 2)-(Part 7) are the same [Tone] blocks at 02 01 00 00, 02 02 00 00, … 02 06 00 00
coverage.drumKit: complete: the Temporary Drum Kit (03 00 00 00), all 88 keys (21-108), each with its partial and its partial EQ
coverage.drumKitInst: Inst Common only: the [Drum Kit Inst] offset table (p16) lists Inst Pitch Env (03 30 02 00), Inst Filter Env (03 30 03 00) and Inst Amp Env (03 30 04 00) as tables of those names, which the manual never prints
coverage.sequencer: not laid out: Scene Sequencer (eight [Sequencer] blocks, 01 00 37 00 - 01 00 45 00, two apart) is printed as one unnumbered name eight times, so no path can name one; Scene Sequencer Data (eight [Sequencer Data] blocks of 4,096 bytes of step data, 01 00 47 00 - 01 02 27 00, 00 20 00 apart) is a pattern, not an edit-buffer setting
